chunks.content: ## Core Tool: Sewing in CLO This section explains how to use the core sewing tools in CLO, including automatic sewing, manual sewing lines, and free sewing. It covers tool selection, sewing line creation, sewing direction, and simulation functions essential for garment construction. ### Using the Automatic Sewing Tool The automatic sewing tool in CLO adds sewing lines based on garment type, simplifying the initial sewing setup. - Open the library and navigate to **Connect the Cloud Training > Core Tool > Automatic Sewing**. - Double-click to open the tool, then close the library. - Load the garment (e.g., a T-shirt arranged in the workspace). - Select the automatic sewing tool. - Click the small triangle next to the garment to select the garment type: top, pants, or skirt. - Choose the desired part (e.g., top and front skirt). - Select the sewing line type (e.g., 5) and specify the side (left or back). - Click **OK** to automatically add sewing lines. - Rotate the 3D interface to verify sewing line placement. - Press **Ctrl + ` (grave accent key)** to simulate garment wearing, applying sewing and gravity functions. - Press **Ctrl + `** again to stop simulation. ### Manual Sewing Tools Overview Manual sewing tools allow precise control over sewing line placement in both 2D and 3D windows. - Open the library and select the core sewing tool. - Confirm and close the library. - Sewing tools are available in both the 2D and 3D toolbar, enabling sewing in either view. - There are three main sewing tools: - **Sewing Tool (Line-to-Line Sewing):** Connects two lines with a sewing line. - **Free Sewing Tool:** Allows sewing between any two points, not strictly along garment outlines. - **M to N Sewing Tool:** Connects multiple lines on one side (M lines) to multiple lines on the other (N lines). ### Creating Sewing Lines with the Sewing Tool - Select the sewing tool. - In 2D or 3D, click one side of a pattern line, then click the corresponding line on the other side to create a sewing line. - Sewing lines have direction indicators (short marks). Ensure directions match to avoid intersections. - For multiple lines, select one line, then hold **Shift** and select additional lines without releasing **Shift**. - The selected lines turn light green, indicating readiness for sewing. - Click the corresponding lines on the opposite side while still holding **Shift**. - After all pairs are selected, release **Shift** to complete sewing. - If a sewing line is added incorrectly, use **Backspace** to delete it or **Ctrl + Z** to undo the last action. - Always verify sewing line directions to prevent twisted seams. ### Free Sewing Tool Usage - Switch to the free sewing tool from the toolbar. - Click the start point anywhere on the garment to begin a sewing line. - Click the end point to complete the sewing line. - This tool is flexible and does not require sewing along pattern outlines.

chunks.content: - If a sewing line is added incorrectly, use **Backspace** to delete it or **Ctrl + Z** to undo the last action. - Always verify sewing line directions to prevent twisted seams. ### Free Sewing Tool Usage - Switch to the free sewing tool from the toolbar. - Click the start point anywhere on the garment to begin a sewing line. - Click the end point to complete the sewing line. - This tool is flexible and does not require sewing along pattern outlines. - For multiple lines (M to N free sewing): - Select all M lines, then press **Backspace** to confirm. - Select all N lines, press **Backspace** to finish. - Maintain consistent sewing line direction during selection. - Incorrect sewing directions can be corrected by deleting and re-adding lines. ### Editing Sewing Lines and Directions - Use the **Edit Sewing Line Tool** to select and modify existing sewing lines. - To delete a sewing line, select it and press the **Delete** key. - To flip the sewing direction, right-click the selected sewing line and choose **Switch Sewing Line**. - Flipping directions resolves intersection and twisting issues in seams. ### Checking Sewing Line Length and Accuracy - Use the **Check Length of Sewing Line Tool** to verify sewing line compatibility. - This tool measures: - **Length Difference:** The absolute difference in length between paired sewing lines. - **Proportion Difference:** The relative percentage difference. - Default acceptable length difference is 5 mm. - If length difference exceeds this, the sewing line is highlighted with a red rough line as a warning. - Adjust length or proportion thresholds as needed to fit garment requirements. - This verification prevents sewing errors and ensures proper fit. --- ## Types of Sewing Lines and Seam Attributes This section covers the classification of sewing lines, seam attributes in CLO, and how to adjust them for garment construction and simulation. ### Accessing Sewing Line Types - Press **Y** to open the Sketchbook. - Double-click the core tool related to sewing line types. - Close the Sketchbook to return to the workspace. ### Understanding Seam Panels and Simulation - Sewing lines connect panels that overlap at seams. - In the 2D window, select all sewing lines using the **Edit Sewing Line Tool**. - In the attribute editor, you can find seam properties. - Click on the seam attribute and press **Ctrl + `** to simulate. - The seam panel flattens during simulation, showing how fabric layers interact. ### Overlapping Sewing Lines for Layered Garments - For garments with multiple layers (e.g., two-layer rawhide sleeves), sewing lines must overlap properly. - Overlap sewing lines by adjusting the panel folds and ensuring correct layering. - Use fold tools to open or close panels as needed for proper assembly. - This technique is critical for styles requiring layered or complex seam arrangements.
